title: Week 24: /cd command and nested sub-agents
description: Claude Code v2.1.166–v2.1.176 released June 8–12, 2026. Key features include /cd to move sessions to new working directories without rebuilding prompt cache, sub-agents can now spawn their own sub-agents (capped at five levels deep), --safe-mode for troubleshooting, and fallbackModel configuration.

community_feedback.quote: Starting June 15, 2026, Agent SDK and claude -p usage on subscription plans will draw from a new monthly Agent SDK credit
The post-June 15 pricing would significantly affect heavy users of non-interactive Claude features
Users discussing potentially 10x price increases under the new plan for certain usage patterns

title: June 2026: /automate skill, enhanced cloud agents, and improved Bugbot
description: Cursor's June 2026 update introduces the /automate skill for creating automations directly in agent sessions, new GitHub and Slack triggers, cloud environment setup in under 10 minutes, cloud subagents with /in-cloud, and Bugbot performance improvements (3x faster, 22% cheaper, finds 10% more bugs). Published June 22, 2026.

title: Copilot CLI GA, Agent Finder, Auto Mode, and Claude Fable 5
description: June 2026 updates include Copilot CLI new terminal interface generally available (June 23), Agent Finder for GitHub Copilot (June 17), Auto Mode available for all users (June 17), Copilot app support for BYOK (June 23), Claude Fable 5 generally available (June 9), and numerous enhancements to Copilot code review, chat context, and enterprise features.

title: June 2026: Session folders, automations, and Devin Review enhancements
description: Devin's June 2026 updates include session folders for organization, !ultra and !fast mid-session toggles, smarter emoji reactions, custom OAuth for marketplace MCP servers, Devin Review improvements with pending PR cancellations on new commits, large paste auto-attach, personal automations, and numerous enterprise features including default member roles and V3 API enhancements.

community_feedback.quote: Devin didn't fail because the ambition was wrong. It failed because it aimed at a version of autonomy current models can't yet support
Keeping AI model set to 'Adaptive' for best value ($20). Notes decent daily and weekly limits
Most AI coding tools wait until you ask for help, but Devin's approach is different - runs the work nobody wants
